q:
Consider the following statements about material released from a job (e.g., during POH):
1. Serviceable released material is returned to the stores depot, taken into stock and credited to the job at its assessed value.
2. Unserviceable released material is treated as scrap and disposed of through the stores depot.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Unserviceable material released from workshop jobs is disposed of as scrap:

options.A: Immediately by the worker who removed it
options.B: By the shop incharge at his discretion, without any record
options.C: By debiting its value to the next job taken up
options.D: Only after it is condemned under the orders of the competent authority and returned to the stores depot

q: The cost of work done by a workshop for another railway is recovered:

options.A: In cash from the other railway's workshop cash office
options.B: Through transfer transactions (Account Current) between the accounts offices of the two railways
options.C: By debiting the work finally to the home railway's revenue head
options.D: By adjustment against stores supplied by that railway, in all cases

q: When a partly executed job is transferred from one workshop to another, the cost already accumulated on the job is:

options.A: Written off to shop on-cost of the transferring workshop
options.B: Passed on to the receiving workshop through transfer entries, so that the total cost of the job remains ascertainable
options.C: Recovered from the staff of the transferring workshop
options.D: Ignored, and the receiving workshop starts costing the job afresh from the beginning

q: Work executed in a railway workshop for another Government department is charged at:

options.A: Cost only, with no addition of any kind
options.B: Cost plus the prescribed departmental charges
options.C: Double the cost of the job
options.D: A nominal charge of one rupee per job

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Depreciation of workshop plant and buildings enters the cost of jobs notionally, as proforma on-cost.
2. The cost of ordinary repairs and maintenance of workshop plant is an actual charge borne under on-cost.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Depreciation enters workshop job costing only as a notional (proforma) charge, and not as a cash payment by the workshop.
2. In the railway's financial books, depreciation on workshop assets is provided by a cash payment made by the workshop every month.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: If the cost of a workshop job is likely to exceed the sanctioned estimate, the excess expenditure requires:

options.A: Sanction of a revised estimate by the competent authority
options.B: No sanction, as workshop jobs are exempt from estimate control
options.C: Only a verbal approval of the shop incharge
options.D: Adjustment against savings on some other job, without any sanction

q:
Consider the following statements about the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense budget:
1. It provides for the gross expenditure (debits) expected to be booked on jobs during the year.
2. It also provides for the credits expected from outturn transferred to Stores, Revenue or Capital heads during the year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Expenditure under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense in a workshop can be incurred only:

options.A: Up to the cash balance available in the workshop imprest
options.B: Against the personal guarantee of the Workshop Accounts Officer
options.C: Without any budget provision, since it is a suspense head
options.D: Within the budget allotment and against duly sanctioned work orders/estimates

q: The average unit cost of Periodic Overhaul for a period is computed as:

options.A: Total POH outlay divided by the number of shops in the workshop
options.B: Total POH outlay divided by the number of units turned out in the period
options.C: Total material cost divided by the number of units programmed for the next year
options.D: Total POH outlay divided by the total staff of the workshop

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Unit costs of Periodic Overhaul are compared between workshops and with those of previous periods as a measure of cost control.
2. Such comparison is confined to shops within the same workshop and is never made with other workshops.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The annual POH programme of a repair workshop is fixed mainly with reference to:

options.A: The leave roster of workshop staff
options.B: The stores purchase programme of the railway
options.C: The number of visitors expected at the workshop
options.D: The arisings of stock due for overhaul and the capacity of the workshop

q: Which of the following correctly states the reconciliation of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense for a year?

options.A: Opening work-in-progress + expenditure booked during the year = outturn transferred out + closing work-in-progress
options.B: Opening work-in-progress + outturn transferred out = expenditure booked during the year + closing work-in-progress
options.C: Expenditure booked during the year = closing work-in-progress only
options.D: Outturn transferred out = opening work-in-progress only

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. If the outlay (expenditure booked) in a period exceeds the outturn transferred out, the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense increases.
2. If the outturn transferred out in a period exceeds the outlay, the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense decreases.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Transactions between two accounting units (e.g., a workshop and another accounting unit) that are settled through the Account Current instead of by cash payment are known as:

options.A: Suspense transactions
options.B: Deposit transactions
options.C: Remittance transactions
options.D: Transfer transactions

q: Clearance of amounts from Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is effected:

options.A: In one lump sum at the end of the year, for all jobs together
options.B: Only when the Railway Board specifically orders it
options.C: Job-wise, on completion of each job, on the basis of the completion report/outturn statement
options.D: By transferring all debits to shop on-cost every month

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. No balance should remain under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense against a job whose outturn has been fully transferred to the final head.
2. Outstanding items under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense are never reviewed after the annual accounts are closed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Before an article is taken up for manufacture in a railway workshop instead of being purchased, a comparison is generally made between:

options.A: The direct labour cost of manufacture and the market price
options.B: The full cost of manufacture, including proforma on-cost, and the market/purchase price
options.C: The material cost of manufacture and the market price
options.D: The shop on-cost of manufacture and the market price

q: If, for a particular job, the outturn transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense exceeds the total cost booked on that job, it indicates:

options.A: An abnormal credit on the job, pointing to an error (e.g., charges booked to a wrong work order or excess transfer) requiring investigation
options.B: A profit earned by the workshop on that job in the normal course
options.C: That the job should be reopened and more material issued to it
options.D: That the excess should be credited to the Pension Fund

q:
Consider the following statements about the allowed time under the incentive scheme:
1. An allowed time, once fixed after work study, is not revised merely because workers earn high bonus on the job.
2. An allowed time is liable to revision when there is a change in the method of work, machine or process.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Where a measured job is executed jointly by a gang of workers under the incentive scheme, the bonus earned on the job is distributed among the members of the gang:

options.A: In proportion to the time wages of each member
options.B: Equally among all members, irrespective of their wages
options.C: To the gang leader alone, who distributes it at his discretion
options.D: In proportion to the seniority of the members

q: For a new operation for which no allowed time has so far been fixed, the work is generally started:

options.A: Only after continuous time study spread over a full year
options.B: Without any time standard, bonus being paid at the shop average rate
options.C: On the allowed time of some other operation selected by the chargeman
options.D: On a provisional allowed time, which is confirmed or revised after proper work study

q: Incentive bonus earned by a workshop worker is:

options.A: Paid in cash on the day each job is completed
options.B: Computed on the jobs completed during the month and paid along with the monthly wages
options.C: Credited to the worker's Provident Fund account
options.D: Paid annually along with the Productivity Linked Bonus

q: Under the Group Incentive Scheme, the target outturn of a group for a period is fixed mainly with reference to:

options.A: The total earnings of the workshop in the previous year
options.B: The number of machines installed in the shop
options.C: The sanctioned strength of the group and the allowed-time norms for the units to be turned out
options.D: The outturn of the best-performing group of the workshop

q: If the accepted outturn of a group in a period falls short of the target fixed under the Group Incentive Scheme, the consequence is that:

options.A: The group still receives the full bonus at the target rate
options.B: The members are fined an amount equal to the value of the shortfall
options.C: The shortfall is ignored and the same target bonus is paid
options.D: The group incentive is correspondingly reduced, and below the prescribed minimum level of outturn no incentive is payable

q: The Production Control Organisation (PCO) of a workshop is primarily responsible for:

options.A: Planning and scheduling the production/repair programme and controlling the flow of work through the shops
options.B: Maintaining the accounts of the workshop
options.C: Purchasing the stores required by the workshop
options.D: Fixing and paying the wages of workshop staff

q: The 'progress' or follow-up function in production control consists of:

options.A: Preparing the annual budget of the workshop
options.B: Chasing and expediting jobs and materials through the successive shops so that the programme is not held up
options.C: Inspecting the finished articles for quality
options.D: Maintaining the gate attendance cards of staff

q: Machine loading charts/statements prepared by the production control organisation show:

options.A: The wages paid to the operators of each machine
options.B: The power consumed by each machine during the month
options.C: The work loaded on the machines/groups against their available capacity, bringing out overloading or underloading
options.D: The scrap generated on each machine

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Production control — routing, scheduling, dispatching and follow-up — is a planning and control function, distinct from the actual execution of the work in the shops.
2. Shops are free to take up operations in any sequence and priority, irrespective of the production programme.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The machine-hour rate of a machine (or a group of similar machines) is arrived at by dividing:

options.A: The original cost of the machine by its expected life in years
options.B: The total wages of the shop by the number of machines
options.C: The total material cost of the shop by the machine hours
options.D: The total expenses attributable to the machine for a period by the effective machine hours worked in that period

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Standing charges of a machine, such as depreciation and insurance, are incurred whether the machine works or remains idle.
2. Running charges of a machine, such as power consumed and consumable stores, vary broadly with the hours the machine actually runs.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Machine utilisation in a workshop is generally expressed as:

options.A: The ratio of the machine hours actually worked to the total machine hours available in the period
options.B: The ratio of breakdown hours to the hours worked
options.C: The number of jobs completed per machine per month
options.D: The ratio of operators employed to the machines installed

q: Prolonged idleness of machines in a shop affects the cost of the workshop's outturn because:

options.A: Idle machines earn incentive bonus for their operators
options.B: The fixed charges of the idle machines have to be spread over the jobs actually done, raising the on-cost burden on the outturn
options.C: Material issued to jobs automatically increases
options.D: Idle machines are written off from the Plant Register

q: Electric power consumed by the different shops of a workshop is charged to the respective shops:

options.A: Equally among all shops, by dividing the total bill by the number of shops
options.B: As part of each shop's on-cost, on the basis of meter readings where meters are provided
options.C: Directly to individual jobs in proportion to their material cost
options.D: To the capital head of the workshop

q: Where separate meters for power are not provided in the shops, the workshop's power charges are apportioned among the shops generally on the basis of:

options.A: The connected load (total horse power/kilowatts of the machines installed) of each shop
options.B: The number of workers employed in each shop
options.C: The floor area occupied by each shop
options.D: The value of outturn of each shop

q: The cost of power for general lighting of the workshop, which cannot be attributed to any particular shop, is charged to:

options.A: Shop on-cost of the largest shop
options.B: The jobs under execution during night hours
options.C: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.D: General on-cost of the workshop

q: Every item of machinery and plant installed in a workshop is recorded, with its cost and particulars, in:

options.A: The Plant Register, under a distinctive plant number allotted to each machine
options.B: The Workshop General Register
options.C: The stores price ledger
options.D: The completion report book

q: Repairs to a shop's machinery executed by another shop of the same workshop (e.g., electrical repairs by the electrical shop) are booked on work orders, and the cost is ultimately borne:

options.A: By the executing shop, as the cost of its own jobs
options.B: By the stores depot which supplied the material
options.C: By the shop owning the machine, as part of its on-cost
options.D: By debit to Capital, in all cases

q: Rolling stock sanctioned under the Rolling Stock Programme but manufactured in a railway workshop is executed on capital work orders, and on completion the compiled cost is transferred:

options.A: To the revenue working expenses of the workshop
options.B: To the Capital head (or the Depreciation Reserve Fund, where the item is provided as a replacement under the programme)
options.C: To the Stores Suspense head
options.D: To the Pension Fund

q: Wagons manufactured in a workshop as replacements of condemned wagons are charged on completion to:

options.A: Capital, like all newly built wagons
options.B: Revenue working expenses
options.C: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, permanently
options.D: The Depreciation Reserve Fund, the wagons being renewals/replacements of condemned stock

q: The decision whether an overaged rolling stock unit should be put through an extensive repair or be condemned and replaced is guided largely by a comparison of:

options.A: The scrap value realisable from the unit alone
options.B: The estimated cost of the repair, together with the residual life it would give, as compared with the cost of a new unit
options.C: The original purchase price of the unit alone
options.D: The labour cost of the repair only

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure on repairs which merely restore a unit to its original condition is charged to the Periodic Overhaul (revenue) work orders.
2. The cost of additional fittings or improvements provided during an overhaul, not forming part of restoration, is charged to separate capital/DRF work orders.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The cost of rectifying (reworking) articles rejected for bad workmanship is accounted for:

options.A: As cost of defective work charged to the shop on-cost, so that the legitimate cost of the job is not inflated
options.B: As a normal addition to the cost of the original job
options.C: As a recovery from the Provident Fund of the worker concerned
options.D: As capital expenditure of the workshop

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rejection in the shops, even when far beyond the normal process limits, is loaded wholly on the cost of the good output.
2. Abnormal rejection beyond normal limits is investigated, and its cost, less the scrap value realised, is treated as a loss/on-cost item rather than being loaded on good production.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The tool room of a workshop functions as a service shop; consequently its working expenses are:

options.A: Charged directly to the individual jobs of the production shops
options.B: Apportioned among the shops served by it, forming part of their on-cost burden
options.C: Debited to Stores Suspense
options.D: Borne directly by the Railway Board

q: Under the tool check system followed in workshops, tools issued to a worker:

options.A: Become the personal property of the worker
options.B: Are never required to be returned to the tool room
options.C: Are issued only against a cash deposit, in all cases
options.D: Are recorded against the worker's name/check (tool loan account) and are returnable, the worker remaining responsible for their custody

q: In the production of castings in a foundry, the role of the pattern prepared in the pattern shop is that:

options.A: The pattern is used to form the mould (the impression in the moulding sand) from which the casting takes its shape
options.B: The pattern is melted along with the metal charge in the cupola
options.C: The pattern is the finished casting itself
options.D: The pattern is used only for painting the castings

q: For castings required repeatedly in large numbers, metal patterns are generally preferred to wooden patterns because:

options.A: Metal patterns are cheaper to make in the first instance
options.B: Wooden patterns cannot be used for sand moulding at all
options.C: Metal patterns need no pattern shop for their upkeep
options.D: Metal patterns are more durable and retain their dimensions over long and repeated use

q: Foundry costing is generally expressed in terms of:

options.A: Cost per casting, irrespective of its size or weight
options.B: Cost per moulding box used in the foundry
options.C: Cost per unit weight (e.g., per kilogram or per tonne) of good castings produced
options.D: Cost per worker employed in the foundry

q: Melting loss (loss of metal by oxidation etc. during melting in the cupola/furnace) has the effect of:

options.A: Increasing the metal cost that has to be borne by the good castings produced
options.B: Reducing the cost of the castings
options.C: Being recovered in full as scrap from the furnace
options.D: Being charged to the pattern shop as its on-cost

q: The charge fed into a foundry cupola normally consists of:

options.A: Finished castings and moulding sand
options.B: Pig iron, foundry returns/scrap and coke as fuel, together with flux as required
options.C: New steel billets only
options.D: Coal tar and lubricating oil only

q: When a job passes from one shop to another within the same workshop in the course of its execution:

options.A: The work order is closed in the first shop and a fresh work order is opened in the next shop
options.B: The cost accumulated up to that stage is transferred out to the final head of account
options.C: The job remains under the same work order and continues under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense until its final completion
options.D: The job is treated as completed at the end of each shop's operation

q: Work orders issued for jobs executed on behalf of other railways/units (foreign work) distinctly indicate:

options.A: The name of the chargeman who will supervise the job
options.B: The market price expected for the finished article
options.C: The date of the next audit inspection of the workshop
options.D: The allocation (head of account) of the indenting railway or unit to which the cost of the job is debitable

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Jobs executed by a workshop for its own railway are called 'foreign' work.
2. The cost of foreign work is finally borne by the executing workshop and is not recovered from the indenting railway/unit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Age analysis of the balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, carried out at the periodical suspense review, classifies the outstanding jobs according to:

options.A: The period for which each job or work order has remained open, so that the oldest outstanding items are identified for clearance
options.B: The trade of the workers employed on the jobs
options.C: The type of material consumed on the jobs
options.D: The names of the shop incharges concerned

q: A work order against which no expenditure has been booked for a long period and which is lying dormant is dealt with at the suspense review by:

options.A: Automatically writing off its balance to revenue
options.B: Transferring its balance to the oldest running job of the shop
options.C: Calling for the reasons for the stoppage, and either expediting its completion or closing it under competent orders
options.D: Omitting it from all future suspense reviews

q: Jobs which have been physically completed but whose cost has not yet been transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense are, at the suspense review:

options.A: Shown as jobs in progress in the ordinary course
options.B: Charged to shop on-cost
options.C: Deleted from the Workshop General Register
options.D: Specifically listed and pursued for prompt transfer of the outturn, since their pendency inflates the suspense balance

q: Under the incentive scheme, allowed times for jobs are fixed:

options.A: Operation-wise, for the successive operations of a job as shown in the operation/route sheet
options.B: Only for the job as a whole, and never for individual operations
options.C: By the workers themselves, operation by operation
options.D: Only for work done in the workshop office

q: In shops where production is predominantly machine-based, on-cost may be absorbed on jobs on the basis of:

options.A: The direct material cost of the jobs
options.B: The number of workers present in the shop
options.C: The floor area occupied by each job
options.D: The machine hours worked on the jobs, through a machine-hour rate

q: A machine history card/register maintained for each machine in a workshop records, among other things:

options.A: Only the date of installation of the machine
options.B: Its breakdowns and the repairs carried out on it, which helps in judging whether its continued repair remains economical
options.C: The wages paid to its operator each month
options.D: The jobs reserved for the machine in the next year

q: Runners, risers and defective castings of the foundry which are fit for re-melting are treated as:

options.A: Finished goods issued to the stores depot
options.B: Losses written off without any credit to the foundry
options.C: Foundry returns, credited to the foundry at scrap value and used again in the cupola charge
options.D: Items sold directly to the public by the foundry

q: Patterns retained in the pattern store for future repeat orders are recorded in a pattern register, and the cost of their upkeep/preservation is borne:

options.A: By the stores depot, as part of the stock value
options.B: By the pattern shop, as an on-cost (period) charge
options.C: By the foundry workers, personally
options.D: By debit to Capital, every year

q: In the age-wise analysis of outstanding workshop jobs, the outstandings are typically grouped:

options.A: By the size of the outstanding balance alone
options.B: By the alphabetical order of the job titles
options.C: By the colour of the work order forms used
options.D: By age bands (e.g., under 3 months, 3-6 months, 6-12 months and over one year), so that the oldest items receive attention first

q: In production control, 'dispatching' means:

options.A: Sending the finished goods to the stores depot
options.B: Preparing the annual production programme of the workshop
options.C: Releasing work to the shops/machines in the planned sequence and priority, i.e., putting the schedule into operation
options.D: Inspecting the jobs after their completion

q: Work orders in a railway workshop are classified and numbered with reference to:

options.A: The trade of the leading worker on the job
options.B: The head of account/allocation (Capital, DRF or Revenue) to which the cost of the job is chargeable
options.C: The estimated duration of the job
options.D: The stores depot supplying the material

q: On-cost rates in force in a workshop are required to be revised when:

options.A: A new shop is added to the workshop
options.B: The workshop changes its weekly holiday
options.C: A new Workshop Accounts Officer assumes charge
options.D: The actual on-cost incurred differs widely and persistently from the on-cost absorbed on jobs

q: The salaries of shop supervisory staff such as foremen and chargemen, who supervise work generally and cannot be booked to individual jobs, are charged to:

options.A: Shop on-cost
options.B: The first job taken up each day
options.C: The Capital head of the workshop
options.D: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense as direct labour

q: The cost of inspection and testing of workshop outturn by staff not booked to individual jobs is treated as:

options.A: A direct charge on each article inspected
options.B: A recovery from the stores depot
options.C: An item of on-cost of the shop/workshop
options.D: A charge to the Capital head

q: The expenses of the drawing and design office of a workshop, which serves the workshop as a whole, form part of:

options.A: Shop on-cost of the erecting shop only
options.B: General on-cost of the workshop
options.C: The cost of the first job designed
options.D: Stores Suspense

q: Where a workshop generates its own electric power, the cost of running the power house is distributed among the shops:

options.A: On the basis of the power consumed by each shop
options.B: Equally among all shops, irrespective of consumption
options.C: On the basis of the number of workers in each shop
options.D: On the basis of the material cost of each shop

q: Essential indirect workers attached to a shop under the incentive scheme (such as helpers and crane operators), whose individual output cannot be measured, are paid incentive bonus:

options.A: At a flat rate fixed by the shop incharge
options.B: Only when the shop completes its annual programme
options.C: Linked to the average bonus earned by the direct workers of the shop
options.D: At double the rate of direct workers

q: For incentive purposes, the output of a worker or shop is expressed in terms of:

options.A: Machine hours booked
options.B: Number of requisitions issued
options.C: Wages paid during the period
options.D: Standard hours, i.e., the total allowed time for the work actually turned out

q: In time study for fixing allowed times, the observed time taken by a worker is converted into normal time by:

options.A: Applying the rating factor, which relates the worker's pace of working to the normal pace
options.B: Adding the total idle time of the shop
options.C: Dividing it by the number of workers in the gang
options.D: Adopting the time taken by the slowest worker

q: Work sampling, as a technique of work measurement, consists of:

options.A: Continuous stop-watch observation of one worker for a full shift
options.B: Timing only the fastest operation in a shop
options.C: Making a large number of random instantaneous observations to determine the proportion of time spent on various activities
options.D: Asking workers to report their own timings

q: Allowed times for repetitive operations in a workshop can be built up without a fresh stop-watch study on every occasion by using:

options.A: The timings of the previous year's overhaul programme
options.B: Standard data / predetermined motion time systems compiled from past work studies
options.C: Estimates given by the stores depot
options.D: The average of the wages paid on similar jobs

q: For compiling the cost of Periodic Overhaul unit-wise, the arrangement followed in a repair workshop is that:

options.A: One common work order is used for all units overhauled in a year
options.B: POH cost is compiled only shop-wise and never unit-wise
options.C: Units are grouped class-wise under a single work order for the whole year
options.D: A distinct work order is allotted to each unit of rolling stock taken up for overhaul

q: The periodicity at which rolling stock is taken up for Periodic Overhaul is prescribed by:

options.A: The Railway Board
options.B: The Workshop Accounts Officer
options.C: The shop incharge of the repair shop
options.D: The stores depot attached to the workshop

q: Intermediate Overhaul (IOH) of rolling stock is:

options.A: The same as Periodic Overhaul, by another name
options.B: An overhaul carried out only after an accident
options.C: A lighter overhaul carried out between two Periodic Overhauls to keep the stock in serviceable condition
options.D: An overhaul carried out only in production units

q: Mid-Life Rehabilitation (MLR) of coaches, carried out in workshops, is aimed at:

options.A: Converting passenger coaches into parcel vans
options.B: Extending the service life of the coach by heavy mid-life repairs and renewal of fittings
options.C: Reducing the tare weight of the coach
options.D: Repainting the coach in a new livery only

q: Corrosion repairs to the body of a coach, carried out during its overhaul in a workshop, are:

options.A: Charged to Capital as an improvement
options.B: Charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund in all cases
options.C: Recovered from the passengers through a surcharge
options.D: Treated as part of the overhaul cost chargeable to revenue

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cost of repairing accident-damaged rolling stock so as to restore it to service is charged to revenue working expenses.
2. Where accident-damaged stock is condemned and replaced by new stock, the cost of the new stock is charged to Capital/the Depreciation Reserve Fund, as applicable.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A machine in a workshop which is beyond economical repair is dealt with by:

options.A: Condemning it under the orders of the competent authority and removing it from the Plant Register
options.B: Keeping it in the Plant Register permanently at full value
options.C: Transferring it to the stores depot as serviceable stock
options.D: Charging its full original cost to shop on-cost
